header:
Nvidia hits $5.7T
What it means for you

lines.text: Nvidia touched about $5.7 trillion. Index funds own a slice.
lines.say: Nvidia touched five point seven trillion. Index funds own a slice.

lines.text: Fri, Oct 2, 2026: shares hit a record high during trading, the first since May.
lines.say: On Friday, October second, the stock hit its first record high since May.

scene.headline: Nvidia hits first record since May

lines.text: Year-end 2022: about $360 billion. Oct 2, 2026 peak: about $5.7 trillion. Roughly 16x.
lines.say: At the end of twenty twenty-two it was worth about three hundred sixty billion. That's roughly sixteen times bigger.

lines.text: Earlier: a 2-month slide (May-July) erased over $1 trillion. Sep 28: a record $150B added to its buyback plan.
lines.say: First, a two-month slide erased over a trillion dollars. Then Nvidia added a record one hundred fifty billion to its buyback plan.

lines.text: Nvidia is about 8% of the S&P 500 (Sep 2026), the biggest single-stock weight since at least 1981.
lines.say: If you own an S and P five hundred fund, this is your money too. Nvidia is about eight percent of it.

lines.text: In an S&P 500 index fund, about $8 of every $100 sits in Nvidia.
lines.say: So in an S and P five hundred fund, about eight dollars of every hundred sits in this one stock.

lines.text: Example: if Nvidia fell 10%, 8% x 10% = about a 0.8% drop for an S&P 500 fund, from Nvidia alone.
lines.say: It cuts both ways. For example, if Nvidia fell ten percent, that alone would pull an S and P fund down about point eight percent.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.
